visual_thesis: Keep a workflow’s trigger and destination stable while replacing a model step; use the same input and expected-output test to judge the change, with data-policy differences visible.
mechanism_metaphor: One continuous sectional workflow rail runs from a labeled Webinar transcript leaf through a detachable model joint to a Blog draft leaf. The joint is lifted slightly above its empty socket, exposing two differently keyed but unbranded alternate model inserts. The rail, trigger notch and destination remain aligned underneath. Beneath the main rail, one test strip has a source case labeled Same input and a separate criterion leaf labeled Expected output; a headless comparison brace associates them with the output, not a training arrow. A lower detached policy seam labeled Check data rules is distinct from workflow behavior. Twelve meaningful roles: transcript leaf, stable rail, trigger notch, model socket, installed insert, two alternate inserts, output connection, blog-draft leaf, input test case, expected criterion leaf, comparison brace and policy seam. No model brand logos, invented compatibility guarantee, switch controls, success marks, fake paragraphs or panels.
story_anchors: Source transcript and invariant input test
Stable rail and replaceable model joint with policy seam
Draft destination, expected output and detached vendor caveat

editorial_style_plan.difference_from_earlier_story_images: Unlike the November 20 cyan routing triangle and provider loops, this side section isolates one mechanically removable joint inside an invariant rail, with explicit transcript, draft and expected-output surfaces rather than abstract provider paths.
